## Binding between the identifier and the expected file

| check | result |
|---|---|
| filename matches | True |
| bytes match | True |
| SHA-256 verified | False |
| SHA-256 verifiable here | False |

A hash requires the bytes. The connector returns metadata and an extracted text rendering, never the binary, so the SHA-256 in the brief could not be confirmed or refuted.

The Drive identifier resolves to a file whose name and byte count both equal the brief's expected identity. That is a strong binding and it is NOT proof of content: two files can share a size. The binding is recorded at CONNECTOR_IDENTIFIED, one class below LOCAL_BINARY_HASH_VERIFIED.

## States claimed, and states deliberately not claimed

Claimed: `SOURCE_LOCATED_BY_CONNECTOR`, `SOURCE_CONTENT_PARTIALLY_READ`

Not claimed: `SOURCE_BINARY_LOCAL`, `SOURCE_BINARY_READABLE`, `SOURCE_CONTENT_READ`, `BOUNDARY_CONFIRMED`, `EXTRACTED`

The brief asked for the live status to move to SOURCE_BINARY_LOCAL / SOURCE_BINARY_READABLE / SOURCE_CONTENT_READ. Two of those three are false and the third is only partly true, so none is claimed. Moving the status because a run expected it to move is the exact failure this register exists to prevent.
